title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a base of characteristic p. G is a finite locally free group scheme killed by p; the computations are written for the height-one case, G = Ker(F_H) for a smooth group H. Notation: ω = ω_G (invariant differentials), 𝔤 = Lie G, Π: 𝔤^(p) → 𝔤 the p-th power (restricted Lie) map, and C: ω → ω^(p) its transpose (a Cartier-type operator). ℓ^G is the co-Lie complex (Grothendieck/Illusie) and ℓ̌^{G*} the Lie complex of the Cartier dual G*. Δ*(G) is the Dieudonné crystal of G, or more precisely its two-term 'mod p' version, evaluated on S.

(1) First triangle. The page writes a distinguished triangle ℓ^G[-1] → Δ*(G) → ℓ̌^{G*} → (1), and models it explicitly by two-term complexes in degrees 0 and 1:
- ℓ^G[-1] ≃ [ω^(p) --0--> ω]. This is correct: for G = Ker(F_H), ℓ_G = [ω_{H^(p)} --F*=0--> ω_H].
- Δ*(G) ≃ [ω^(p) --0--> ω^(p)].
- The map between them is (id, C).
- I checked that the mapping cone of (id, C) is quasi-isomorphic to [ω --C--> ω^(p)], i.e. the Lie complex of the dual. The connecting maps (id,0) of degree 1 and (0,id) are as written. So the triangle is a cone triangle and the identification is internally consistent.

(2) Second triangle. This is the Frobenius-twisted version:
- ℓ^{G^(p)}[-1] = [ω^(p) --C^(p)--> ω^(p²)] → [ω^(p) --0--> ω^(p)];
- the third term is [ω^(p²) → ω^(p)], linked by the maps (C, id) and (id,0).

(3) Crystalline formalism. ε: (S/Σ)_cris → S_zar, with a section-type morphism φ satisfying φε = F_S (absolute Frobenius). The note records that Δ*(G) is a crystalline complex carrying F and V, with filtrations whose graded factors are φ*(Q), φ*(P). In addition, Δ*(G) = ε*(Δ(G)) has a filtration with factors P, Q. Here P and Q are the two Hodge pieces, the ω-part and the Lie(G*)-part.

(4) The Dieudonné module. M = 𝔻*(G) = φ*(ω), and M^(p) = φ*(ω^(p)). Then V = φ*(C): M → M^(p), while F = 0, as it should be for a height-one group. So the Dieudonné module of a Frobenius kernel is read off from (ω, C), equivalently from the p-Lie algebra (𝔤, Π).

(5) The complex Δ*(G). It is written Δ*(G) = [ε*M --0--> ε*M] = ε*[M → M]; a struck-out attempt Δ*(G) = ε*(M)° precedes this. The zero differential is what one gets from M ⊗^L Z/p, i.e. [M --p--> M], when pM = 0.

(6) Triangle for general BT_1. [M^(p) --F--> M] → [M --0--> M] → [M --V--> M^(p)], with connecting map (V, id). This is equivalent to the periodic exact sequence … --F--> M^(p)? → M --V--> M^(p) --F--> M → … , i.e. Ker V = Im F and Ker F = Im V. These are the standard exactness properties of the Dieudonné module of a truncated Barsotti–Tate group of level 1.

Purpose. The page is a scratch computation, for the 1970 Montreal-lectures programme on Barsotti–Tate groups and Dieudonné crystals, checking that the crystal of a BT_1 / height-one group is an extension of the Lie complex of G* by the co-Lie complex of G. This is the Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → D(G) → Lie(G*) → 0, here at the level of complexes and made explicit via the Cartier operator.
errors: The orientation of the lower triangle is muddled on the page. The vertex written [M^(p) --V--> M^(p)] should be [M --V--> M^(p)], and the bottom-left vertex should be [M^(p) --F--> M]. Only then are the cone and the labels (V,id), (id,0) consistent with Δ*(G) = [M --0--> M].

Superscript conventions are not used consistently: Δ*(G) is first modelled on ω^(p) and later identified with ε*[M → M], where M = φ*(ω). The roles of φ* versus ε* and of the twists (p) vs (p²) in the second triangle are not fully reconciled. This is a scratch-level inconsistency, not a mathematical error.
The identification ℓ^G[-1] ≃ [ω^(p) --0--> ω] is valid only for height-one G (Frobenius kernels). The page does not state this restriction explicitly.

ideas.what: Co-Lie complex of a height-one group G = Ker F_H computed as [ω^(p) --0--> ω]; Lie complex of the dual as [ω --C--> ω^(p)], with C the transpose of the p-power map Π
ideas.modern_name: co-Lie complex ℓ_G of a finite flat group scheme; restricted Lie algebra / Cartier operator

ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné module of Frobenius kernels / p-Lie algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fontaine; Berthelot–Breen–Messing; classical Dieudonné theory over perfect fields

ideas.what: Δ*(G) = ε*[M --0--> M] for pM = 0 (two-term mod-p Dieudonné complex), with triangle [M^(p) --F--> M] → [M --0--> M] → [M --V--> M^(p)], equivalent to Ker F = Im V and Ker V = Im F
ideas.modern_name: derived reduction M ⊗^L Z/p; exactness of F,V for BT_1 Dieudonné modules

ideas.what: Crystalline topos morphisms ε: S_cris → S_zar and φ with φε = absolute Frobenius, used to compare Frobenius-twisted filtrations (factors φ*Q, φ*P versus P, Q)
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius on crystalline topos / Hodge vs conjugate filtrations

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the mod-p Dieudonné crystal as a two-term complex Δ*(G) = ε*[M --0--> M], with two filtrations (Hodge-type with factors P,Q, and Frobenius-twisted with factors φ*Q, φ*P) intertwined by F and V. This is a complex-level, derived formulation of the Dieudonné crystal of a BT_1. It loosely prefigures derived/prismatic Dieudonné formulations, but it is only sketched here and is standard in substance.
missed.quote: Δ*(G) complexe cristallin avec F, V, filtrations à facteurs φ*(Q), φ*(P) + filtration sur Δ*(G) = ε*(Δ(G)) à facteurs P, Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck worked with complex-level (derived) Dieudonné objects and conjugate/Hodge filtration pairs around 1970. These ideas were later systematized by Illusie, Berthelot–Breen–Messing and, recently, Bhatt–Lurie / Anschütz–Le Bras.

deep.surprise_reason: A competent scratch computation of the Dieudonné crystal of a height-one / BT_1 group via co-Lie complexes and the Cartier operator. All the mathematics is standard and consistent with Grothendieck's published 1970 programme. The derived-complex formulation is a mildly interesting historical detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'ℓ̌^{C*}_· = 𝔩' is most likely ℓ̌^{G*} = ℓ̌, the Lie complex of the Cartier dual G*. The 'C' is a G, and 𝔩 is a script ℓ.
'ℓ^{G^{(p)}}_· = ℓ^{(p)}' and 'ℓ̌^{G*(p)}_· = ℓ̌^{(p)}': the second label also has G*, not C*.
In the lower triangle, the top vertex should read [M --V--> M^(p)] rather than [M^(p) --V--> M^(p)], and the bottom-left vertex is [M^(p) --F--> M].
The final line reads '… --F--> M^(p)? → M --V--> M^(p) → …', i.e. the periodic sequence alternating F and V.
'φε = F_S (frobenius absolu)': the F_S is written over a struck-out letter.
